free_tier.stated: no free tier; KS-3 is USD 30.00 a month for 4 cores and 8 threads, 32 GB of DDR4 ECC RAM and 2 x 480 GB of SSD, and the configure screen sells a Windows Server 2016 Standard 4-core licence as a priced option at USD 34.00 a month, so a Windows-ready box is USD 64.00 a month

retention.stated: the disks persist while the server is rented; the page states no deletion clock

egress.terms: 500 Mbps unmetered on the configure page, against 'Public 300 Mbps' on the KS range table; no byte quota and no overage price is printed on either

interface_detail: a rented dedicated server with a public IPv4 on the machine and a rescue or install path from the OVHcloud manager; RDP once Windows is installed from the licence option
tooling: any RDP client; the OVHcloud manager for install, rescue and billing
chaining: the only row in the sweep with a published licence line item sold apart from the machine, which makes USD 34.00 a month the yardstick every licence-included claim is measured against; the machine is 32 GB of dedicated RAM for USD 30.00, so a workload that needs real memory rather than a vCPU share has no cheaper row.

limits.value: 500 Mbps unmetered per the configure page; 300 Mbps per the range table

limits_note: the two pages disagree on the port: the KS range table says 'Public 300 Mbps' and the configure screen says 500 Mbps unmetered. The configure page is the one that charges the money and is the newer, so it is carried, with the table figure recorded beside it. RAM can be raised to 64 GB for USD 8.90 and the disk comes as 2 x 480 GB SSD or 2 x 2 TB HDD at the same price.

identity_cost.detail: an account and a payment method at order; a card is registered with a small deduction that 'No amount will be charged' and it activates the card, while an order that fails or is cancelled leaves an 'authorisation hold, not a final payment' that clears 'within 15 days for a credit card payment'. Cards accepted are Visa, Mastercard and Maestro, plus PayPal and a prepaid account balance. OVHcloud accounts are region-scoped, and the range table shows this plan orderable from a subset of regions.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the same plan is priced differently on the range table and the configure screen, and the range table shows availability by region rather than everywhere.
confidence_note: the shape, the USD 30.00 base and the USD 34.00 Windows licence option are read from the KS-3 configure screen on 2026-10-26, and the licence is a printed line item rather than a sentence, which is why this record is the anchor for licence cost. Two things are weaker: the port figure contradicts the range table, and the existing catalogue record kimsufi.json prices KS-3 at USD 21.10 from the range page read on 2026-10-22.

evidence.proved: quoted from the configure screen: KS-3 at USD 30.00 a month, 4 cores and 8 threads, 32 GB DDR4 ECC with 64 GB at USD 8.90 more, 2 x 480 GB SSD or 2 x 2 TB HDD, no setup fee shown
the configure page states 500 Mbps unmetered while the KS range table states 'Public 300 Mbps' for the same plan, a contradiction inside the vendor's own site
the range table read four days earlier prints KS-3 at USD 21.10 with 32 GB and 2 x 480 GB, which is the figure carried by compute/kimsufi and does not reproduce on the configure screen read
registering a card makes a small deduction that OVHcloud states is not a charge, and publishes no amount
evidence.quote: A small amount of money is deducted from your bank account to check your card details and their validity.

evidence.proved: an unsuccessful or cancelled order leaves an authorisation hold rather than a payment
evidence.quote: If your order was unsuccessful or was cancelled, the amount shown on your bank account corresponds to an authorisation hold, not a final payment.

evidence.proved: the accepted card networks are Visa, Mastercard and Maestro
evidence.quote: Cards accepted are Visa, Mastercard, Maestro.

notes: The USD 34.00 licence is the number that makes this record useful: it is the only published licence price any lane in the sweep found, and every licence-included claim elsewhere can be read against it. Two disagreements are left standing rather than smoothed. The first is internal: the range table says 300 Mbps public and the configure screen says 500 Mbps unmetered. The second is across records: kimsufi.json carries USD 21.10 for KS-3 from the range page on 2026-10-22 and this record carries USD 30.00 from the configure screen today, so a reader comparing the two should treat the range page as a starting point that moves by region. The all-in figure is USD 64.00, which is 7.89 times the USD 8.11 floor used by the surrounding sweep.

extras.windows_licence: printed: Windows Server 2016 Standard, 4-core, USD 34.00 a month as a configure option

payment_methods.card_at_signup: yes at order, unless the order is paid from a prepaid account balance or by PayPal
payment_methods.debit: accepted, listed with the credit cards under the heading 'Credit/Debit cards': Visa, Mastercard and Maestro, with 3D Secure enabled and the cardholder details matching the account
payment_methods.hold_detail: a card is registered by a small deduction that is not a charge: 'A small amount of money is deducted from your bank account to check your card details and their validity. No amount will be charged'. A failed or cancelled order leaves an 'authorisation hold, not a final payment' that clears 'within 15 days for a credit card payment'. The amount is not published on the payment methods page, the billing FAQ or the payment-method guide.
payment_methods.identity: an account, a card, PayPal or a prepaid account balance; 3D Secure must be enabled and the card details must match the account
